Weston.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Weston calls follow the ground the town sits on: west Fork River (through the town), wooded hills rising around the historic districts, Stonewall Jackson Lake country to the south. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, bats, woodchucks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

In fall and winter, squirrels and rodents push into warm attics across the county, and spring brings denning raccoons looking for chimneys and soffits to raise young. Weston is rich in Victorian and early-1900s homes, brick blocks, and historic asylum-era buildings, with postwar streets around the core. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.
